newsitem.title: USA: US economic panel to hold hearing on CPI/jobs data.
newsitem.headline: US economic panel to hold hearing on CPI/jobs data.

text.p: The Joint Economic Committee on Monday said it plans to hold a hearing on Friday, February 7 to discuss proposals to change the Consumer Price Index as well as the usual monthly discussion of the latest employment data.
The hearing will be held at 0930 EST/1430 GMT, following the release of the January employment report at 0830 EST.
Joint Economic Committee Chairman Jim Saxton has asked for a study from the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics on a proposal to revise the CPI.
A congressionally appointed commission led by Stanford University economist Michael Boskin concluded that the CPI overstates inflation by 1.1 percentage points a year.

The Boskin panel has said the problems with the index are costing the government billions of dollars in overpayment of benefits and lost revenue from improper indexing of programs like Social Security and tax brackets.

Saxton, a Republican from New Jersey, said an analysis by the House and Senate's Joint Economic Committee suggested that almost 40 percent of the budget effects from reducing the CPI would be reflected in tax increases, mostly for middle-income taxpayers.

"A formal BLS response to the Boskin Commission report would permit a more thorough and balanced discussion of CPI issues," Saxton said in a statement. "Let's not rush to judgment before a complete review of the facts."
